findings.title: Governor CONSERVE state never reaches routing; no test bridges governor output -> router/chain input (quota-conservation mode end-to-end is only nominally covered and is in fact broken)
findings.evidence: reconcile_flag (kimi_governor.py:288-321) writes KIMI_LOW_QUOTA.flag ONLY on EXHAUSTED; test_conserve_does_not_write_hard_flag (test_kimi_governor.py:180) confirms CONSERVE writes no flag. The router reads CONSERVE solely from that flag: agent_router.kimi_quota_state (agent_router.py:715-743) returns CONSERVE only for an explicit JSON {"state":"CONSERVE"}. The chain reader _read_kimi_flag_state (agent_chain.py:172-200) likewise only yields CONSERVE from a state= body. Since the governor never emits such a flag under CONSERVE, the router's CONSERVE-narrowing path (agent_router.py:1988-1994) and the chain's CONSERVE critic-only branch (agent_chain.py:298-299) are unreachable via the real governor. Every CONSERVE test injects a hand-authored flag: test_conserve_keeps_only_three_research_task_types_routable_to_kimi (test_agent_router_kimi_lane.py:114), test_conserve_excludes_generic_research_strategy_from_kimi (:131), test_vendor_gate_kimi_conserve_allows_critic_only (test_agent_chain_kimi.py:146). No test runs kimi_governor.evaluate() at a CONSERVE threshold and feeds the resulting on-disk artifact into kimi_quota_state() or _read_kimi_flag_state(). Additionally the governor's real EXHAUSTED body is non-JSON (_write_flag, kimi_governor.py:276-285: 'MANAGED_BY=...\nset_at=...') which agent_router.kimi_quota_state honours only via its fail-closed json.loads-except branch (agent_router.py:735-737), not the documented {"state":...} contract - the two components agree by luck, and no test exercises the governor's actual body against the router parser.
findings.fix: Add an integration test that calls kimi_governor.evaluate() (or reconcile_flag) at NORMAL, CONSERVE, and EXHAUSTED thresholds and asserts the resulting on-disk flag drives agent_router.kimi_quota_state() and agent_chain._read_kimi_flag_state() to the matching state. That test will fail for CONSERVE, forcing the design fix: either have the governor write a CONSERVE-carrying flag (state=CONSERVE body), or give the router a state file/other channel to learn CONSERVE. Also align agent_router.kimi_quota_state to parse the governor's key=value body the way agent_chain._read_kimi_flag_state already does.

findings.title: CONSERVE quota state is unreachable in production — governor clears the flag in CONSERVE, both planes read absent-flag as NORMAL
findings.evidence: reconcile_flag() writes KIMI_LOW_QUOTA.flag ONLY on state=='EXHAUSTED' (line 299); for NORMAL *and* CONSERVE it takes the else branch (line 308) and CLEARs/leaves-absent the flag. The flag is the ONLY thing the two consumers read: agent_router.kimi_quota_state (agent_router.py:727-728) returns NORMAL when the flag is absent, and agent_chain.vendor_gate treats an absent flag as open/NORMAL (_read_kimi_flag_state returns None -> kimi open). So when the real governor computes CONSERVE it removes the flag, and both the router CONSERVE capability-narrowing + task-type gate (agent_router.py route_once/sync) and the chain CONSERVE critic-only narrowing (agent_chain.py vendor_gate kimi branch) are never exercised. The entire CONSERVE machinery in C2 and C3 is dead code in production; it can only be triggered by a hand-written/test flag containing state=CONSERVE. The governor's documented tri-state collapses to bi-state (present=EXHAUSTED / absent=NORMAL) at the flag boundary, silently discarding CONSERVE — the exact 'don't drain a fixed one-month subscription on low-value volume' protection the commits claim.
findings.fix: Make CONSERVE durable at the flag boundary: have reconcile_flag WRITE a flag body carrying state=CONSERVE (JSON {"state":"CONSERVE"} so both consumers parse it — router only accepts JSON, chain accepts JSON or key=value) instead of clearing it, and only clear on NORMAL. Add a router/chain test that drives CONSERVE from an actual governor.evaluate() output rather than a synthetic flag. Alternatively, delete the CONSERVE code paths and document kimi as bi-state, so behaviour matches the docs.

findings.title: QM_StrategyFarm_KimiGovernor_15min task is claimed by CLAUDE.md and the architecture but does not exist and no committed installer creates it
findings.evidence: C6 CLAUDE.md states the kimi lane is 'paced by kimi_governor.py (task QM_StrategyFarm_KimiGovernor_15min)'; KIMI_INTEGRATION_ARCHITECTURE.md:264 and the §15 rollback table (line 386) list the same task as a scheduled spawner. Consequence: the governor runs only reactively as a side effect of kimi_adapter._finalize->kimi_governor.record() on each real call. Time-based transitions with an idle lane are never enforced — in particular the subscription-period-end EXHAUSTED (kimi_governor.compute_state period_ended) will not be written if no call happens after 2026-10-15; the first post-expiry call runs against a dead subscription and only self-heals to EXHAUSTED after 2 consecutive auth failures. The §15 rollback lever 'disable/delete QM_StrategyFarm_KimiGovernor_15min' points at a task that cannot be disabled because it was never installed, and mislabels the governor a 'spawner' (it never spawns kimi).
findings.fix: Either add the governor task to a committed installer (mirror QM_StrategyFarm_AgyGovernor: python kimi_governor.py evaluate every 15min as SYSTEM) and register it, or correct CLAUDE.md/architecture to state the governor is call-driven only and remove the non-existent-task rollback line. findings.title: Fragmented kill switch: QM_KIMI=0 is honored only inside the adapter, not at router routing or chain selection, and is absent from the rollback table

But agent_router never consults QM_KIMI (only KIMI_LOW_QUOTA.flag), so with QM_KIMI=0 the router still ASSIGNS kimi tasks -> they go IN_PROGRESS and then the orchestration slot's adapter call errors, leaving tasks stranded. agent_chain.vendor_gate also never consults QM_KIMI, so the chain still SELECTS kimi, wastes a seat, gets an error, and falls back. Then it disables routing, selection, and execution consistently.

findings.title: Research datasets default to the repo working tree and are not gitignored — dirties the tree and can block Factory_ON minting
findings.evidence: DEFAULT_OUT_ROOT = C:/QM/repo/artifacts/research_datasets. git check-ignore returns nothing for that path (not ignored). Any research/kimi caller that runs observe_projector with the default writes datasets as untracked files into the main repo checkout. Per the runtime-activation flow, Factory_ON minting requires a clean tree including untracked files, and orphan files in the main checkout block fast-forward merges from agent worktrees (Worktree Discipline). The architecture 'keep' list claims 'research intermediates small/off-D:' but this default is on C: inside the repo, uncontrolled.
findings.fix: Point DEFAULT_OUT_ROOT off the repo tree (e.g. D:/QM/research/datasets) or add artifacts/research_datasets/ to .gitignore, and document a retention/cleanup owner for it. Callers should always pass an explicit out_dir outside the checkout.

findings.title: Auto-updater risk only partially mitigated: cli_version is recorded but never pinned or alerted on change
findings.evidence: extract_cli_version stamps the stream-json version banner into every ledger line (verified: live ledger line carries cli_version '0.43.1'), and the parser is deliberately tolerant of new event types. But the kimi CLI auto-updates in place at the pinned PATH and nothing detects or alerts on a version delta between calls; run_agent_orchestration_task.py comments call 'the pinned constant plus the per-run version stamp' the version-pinning defence, yet neither pins an actual version nor warns. A breaking CLI change (e.g. -p/--output-format semantics) degrades silently to status malformed_output, which is NOT in retry_statuses, so calls fail straight to chain fallback / stranded lane tasks with no operator signal beyond a buried ledger field.
findings.fix: Add a governor/heartbeat check that compares the last ledger cli_version against a recorded expected version and raises an OWNER-visible reason (mission control / routing receipt) on change, and consider treating a first-seen new version as a soft-conserve until a smoke passes.

findings.title: Single-flight lock is time-stale-only, not liveness-checked — an orphaned lock wedges the whole kimi lane for up to 2h after an ungraceful kill/reboot
findings.evidence: _acquire_single_flight steals a lock only when its stamp age > stale_s (config single_flight.stale_s=7200s=2h); otherwise it waits wait_s=300s then raises _LockBusy. The lock at D:/QM/strategy_farm/state/kimi_adapter.lock records pid+stamp but the holder's liveness is never checked. If the holding process dies ungracefully (VPS reboot, taskkill), the lock file persists; every subsequent kimi call for up to ~2h waits 300s and returns status error 'single_flight_busy'. No scheduled task cleans this lock; it self-heals only via the 2h stale-steal. Kimi is research-only so impact is bounded (chain falls back), but the lane is silently dead for the window.
findings.fix: On FileExistsError, also steal the lock when the recorded pid is not alive (os.kill(pid,0) / tasklist check) in addition to the stale timeout, and/or shorten stale_s. Optionally clear kimi_adapter.lock in the reboot-diagnostic/at-startup task.

findings.title: Stale/incorrect comments and a referenced config file that does not exist
findings.evidence: command_for(kimi) docstring says '--auto guarantees no interactive prompt hangs a headless run' but the returned argv correctly OMITS --auto (probe battery found --auto is incompatible with -p), and this argv is not even used for execution (run_agent_slot routes kimi to _run_kimi_slot -> kimi_adapter.run_kimi, which builds its own argv). Separately, KIMI_INTEGRATION_ARCHITECTURE.md §7/§8 (lines 240,264) reference config/kimi_governor.v1.json as the governor/subscription-period config, but no such file exists — the governor reads its config from the 'governor' block of config/kimi_adapter.v1.json. These are doc/comment drift that will mislead the next operator doing a rollback or config change.

findings.title: lineage.json schema collision between research_source (C4) and preregister (C5); preregister crashes on a minted artifact
findings.evidence: research_source._lineage_skeleton (research_source.py:433-443) writes lineage.json as {schema:'qm.research-lineage/v1', research_id, version, parent_version_id, discovery_sample, validation_sample, preregistration, mechanization} with NO 'versions' key. preregister._update_lineage (preregister.py:146-168) loads that same file when it exists and does lineage['versions'].append(...) -> KeyError: 'versions'. BOTH modules stamp the identical schema id 'qm.research-lineage/v1' (research_source.py:62, preregister.py:28) on structurally incompatible shapes. The C4 skeleton even reserves a 'preregistration': null slot, i.e. the two are meant to co-locate in the QM-RESEARCH store dir. The intended pre-Q00 path (OBSERVE->...->PRE-REGISTER->STRATEGY CARD, directive sec 9) therefore breaks the first time PRE-REGISTER runs against a real minted artifact. Unexercised by tests: test_research_ledgers.py:98 uses a fresh tmp_path artifact_dir with no pre-existing lineage.json, so the else-branch fabricates {versions:[]} and the KeyError never fires.
findings.fix: Reconcile the lineage.json contract across C4/C5: either (a) give the two shapes distinct schema ids, or (b) make preregister._update_lineage tolerate/upgrade a C4-minted lineage.json (initialise versions=[] when the loaded dict lacks it, and preserve the C4 fields) and confirm both modules agree on whether preregistration versions live in lineage.json['versions'] or in research_source's 'preregistration'/'version'/'parent_version_id' fields. Add a regression test that mints via research_source, then calls preregister.write_preregistration on the same dir.

findings.title: Committed example artifact dataset hash mismatches its manifest and research.json; verify-as-committed would fail, masked only by test re-seal
findings.evidence: The on-disk datasets/DS-2026-0000_projector.json hashes to 02c96c7f4fbe0ed020102e321344c4b09b8c18da6ecf9c618fe95f0c37c4bd40, but both the qm-source-manifest block in source.md AND research.json.computed_outputs[0].sha256 record 2a6b6cca565abe4515152dd295707a5c0b971ce0954c9db00f673b6694f64752. Running research_source.verify against the committed artifact as-is would emit HASH_MISMATCH:datasets/... and NUMERIC_UNBACKED:datasets/... (research_source.py:717-718, 755-756). Every test (test_research_source.py:38-39, test_card_r1_internal_source.py:44-45) copytree's the example then calls rs.seal(), which build_manifest_block recomputes the manifest from the live file (research_source.py:597) BEFORE verify runs, so the stale committed manifest is always overwritten and the mismatch is hidden. This also exposes that verify never cross-checks research.json.computed_outputs[].sha256 against the file or manifest (verify only compares sha256_file(target) to manifest[rel], research_source.py:755); the declared sha256 inside research.json is decorative and can silently diverge, as it does here.
findings.fix: Regenerate the committed worked example so its manifest block and research.json.computed_outputs[].sha256 both equal the actual datasets file hash (run seal and commit the result), so a human reading the canonical example sees a self-consistent artifact. Optionally, have verify also assert research.json.computed_outputs[].sha256 == manifest[rel] so the two recorded hashes cannot disagree undetected.

findings.title: ML-term scan exemption is keyed on the '## Research provenance' heading name, creating a scan blind spot

Runtime-ML prose placed under a heading matching /research provenance/ evades the affirmative ML text scan entirely. This is intended per contract sec 9.4 (a card may truthfully describe ML-assisted discovery), and is mitigated by the unchanged frontmatter r4_ml_forbidden/ml_required check and by mechanization_check's mechanics-section primitives, but the exemption boundary is purely heading-name-based and would not catch a mislabeled section.
findings.fix: Acceptable as designed, but tighten by (a) restricting the exemption to prose only and still scanning any fenced code / parameter / rule block inside the provenance span, or (b) asserting the provenance section contains no mechanical-rule keywords (entry/exit/stop/sizing) so runtime logic cannot hide there.

findings.title: Numeric-provenance only binds declared quantitative_claims; prose numbers with an empty claims list are unbacked-but-passing
findings.evidence: quantitative_claims is listed in _RESEARCH_EMPTY_OK (research_source.py:95-98), so a research.json declaring [] quantitative_claims satisfies presence, and the NUMERIC_UNBACKED loop (research_source.py:759-765) iterates only over declared claims. A number stated only in source.md prose (never entered into quantitative_claims) is therefore never checked against a computed-output hash. This is inherent to any structured-provenance scheme (deterministic code cannot reliably detect every prose number), but it is the residual gap in the 'every quantitative claim cites a computed-output hash' guarantee (directive sec 4.4/R-C).
findings.fix: Document the boundary explicitly (provenance is enforced over declared claims), and consider a heuristic warning when source.md prose outside the provenance/manifest sections contains numeric tokens (%, R, ratios) while quantitative_claims is empty, surfaced to the Critic/preregistration decision rather than as a hard fail.

findings.title: OBSERVE dataset manifest sha256 map is not verified by the downstream consumer
findings.evidence: observe_projector writes a per-file sha256 map + a manifest whose docstring states 'A dataset with a missing sha256 is not consumable (fail closed)' (observe_projector.py:14-22, 387-389). But experiment_memory.project (experiment_memory.py:141-143 via _read_csv) reads gate_outcomes.csv / ea_metrics.csv / idea_families.csv directly from the dataset dir and never opens manifest.json or checks any hash, so the fail-closed-on-missing/mismatched-sha invariant is stated but not enforced at the point of consumption; a hand-edited CSV would be consumed silently.
findings.fix: Have experiment_memory.project (and any other dataset consumer) load manifest.json, verify each CSV's sha256 against the manifest, and refuse (or loudly warn) on mismatch/missing entry before projecting, so the content-addressed guarantee is actually enforced.

findings.title: CONSERVE quota state never reaches either plane — governor writes the flag only on EXHAUSTED
findings.evidence: reconcile_flag (kimi_governor.py:288-321) writes KIMI_LOW_QUOTA.flag ONLY when state=='EXHAUSTED'; on NORMAL/CONSERVE it clears/leaves the flag absent. Test test_kimi_governor.py:180 (test_conserve_does_not_write_hard_flag) locks this in. But both consumers derive quota state SOLELY from that flag: agent_router.kimi_quota_state() returns NORMAL when the flag is absent (agent_router.py, route_once:1909 + the CONSERVE task-type gate at :1994 and the CONSERVE capability narrowing in sync_default_registry:1239); agent_chain.vendor_gate's kimi branch treats an absent flag as open. compute_state() can and does return CONSERVE (kimi_governor.py:216-225), but that state is written only to kimi_governor_state.json, which nothing in either plane reads. Net: the entire CONSERVE machinery (KIMI_CONSERVE_TASK_TYPES gate, KIMI_CONSERVE_CAPABILITIES, chain's CONSERVE critic-only path) is dead in production. With the gemini/agy lane currently auth-degraded (audit drift.md), kimi at cost_rank 12 becomes the cheapest eligible lane for generic research_strategy and will capture it up to 100% before EXHAUSTED fires — the exact F4/R-G failure the design (arch §5.2, §7.2, directive §6) claimed to prevent.
findings.fix: Make kimi_governor.reconcile_flag write the flag on CONSERVE as well as EXHAUSTED, carrying the state; OR have both planes read kimi_governor_state.json (the authoritative state) instead of only the flag. Whichever is chosen must be reconciled with finding #2 (flag body format).

findings.title: KIMI_LOW_QUOTA flag body contract is mutually inconsistent across governor writer, governor ownership-reader, router reader, and chain reader
findings.evidence: Three slices disagree on the flag body format for the SAME file (D:/QM/strategy_farm/KIMI_LOW_QUOTA.flag). (a) Governor writes key=value lines with first line 'MANAGED_BY=kimi_governor' (kimi_governor._write_flag:276-285) and detects its own ownership by that first line (_flag_owned:268-273). (b) Router kimi_quota_state parses the body as JSON only — json.loads(raw) then data.get('state'); any non-JSON body fails closed to EXHAUSTED (agent_router.py, kimi_quota_state, added in commit 4282cea99f). (c) Chain _read_kimi_flag_state accepts JSON {state}, or a key=value 'state=' line, or a MANAGED_BY-only body which it maps to EXHAUSTED (agent_chain.py, added in 2a46f483b9). EXHAUSTED works today only by fail-closed accident (governor's key=value body -> router json.loads fails -> EXHAUSTED; chain finds no state= -> EXHAUSTED). There is NO body the governor can write that expresses CONSERVE and that BOTH consumers honor: the router needs JSON with a 'state' key, but a JSON body would make the governor's own first-line 'MANAGED_BY=' ownership check (_flag_owned) fail. The flag contract cannot carry CONSERVE as currently coded.
findings.fix: Define one canonical flag body (recommend a JSON object carrying both {"managed_by":"kimi_governor","state":"CONSERVE|EXHAUSTED"}); update kimi_governor._write_flag and _flag_owned to write/read ownership from that JSON, update agent_router.kimi_quota_state and agent_chain._read_kimi_flag_state to the same single format, and add an end-to-end test that the governor-written CONSERVE flag actually narrows the router lane and the chain.

findings.title: Adapter repo-mutation guard is repo-only; R-D D:/QM scope and the repo_write receipt contract are not met
findings.evidence: run_kimi computes the critic mutation guard from _repo_porcelain_hash(C:/QM/repo) only (kimi_adapter.py:232-246, before/after at :556 and :606-611). The D:/QM scope mandated by R-D is not implemented: _dir_listing_hash (:249-260) is dead code (never called), and there is no before/after hashing of farm_state.sqlite / D:/QM/strategy_farm/state/ / D:/QM/reports/state/. Consequently the returned repo_write flag reflects repo changes only, but INTERNAL_RESEARCH_SOURCE_CONTRACT.md §4.5 defines critic_receipt.repo_write as 'true if the critic wrote anything to C:/QM/repo OR the D:/QM verdict/evidence paths' and research_source.verify fails closed on it (research_source.py:788). A critic that wrote to D:/QM would yield repo_write=false and pass verify. The named regression test test_critic_write_dqm_state_fails_run (arch §14, contract §12) does not exist in test_kimi_adapter.py. Mitigated (not closed) by the critic agent-file removing Bash/shell.
findings.fix: Extend run_kimi's before/after guard to hash the D:/QM verdict/evidence state paths (reuse the already-written _dir_listing_hash) in addition to the repo porcelain hash, fold both into repo_write, and add test_critic_write_dqm_state_fails_run. If the addendum deliberately narrowed detection to repo-only, then amend contract §4.5/§5.1 and arch §14 to match so the receipt-field semantics and the producer agree.

findings.title: schema_mismatch error class (F9) not implemented — valid-JSON-wrong-schema collapses to malformed_output
findings.evidence: Arch §3.2/§3.4 and the F9 disposition require classifying valid JSON with an unexpected/renamed event set distinctly (error class schema_mismatch) from non-JSON garbage, with test test_stream_json_schema_mismatch_class. The adapter has no STATUS_SCHEMA_MISMATCH constant (status vocab at kimi_adapter.py:55-62); parse_stream_json returns None for both wrong-schema and non-JSON (:103-132); the rc==0-but-unparsed path maps both to STATUS_MALFORMED (:590-591). classify_error patterns (config error_class_patterns) contain only auth_expired/rate_limited. The named test is absent from test_kimi_adapter.py. Fails closed, but the distinct signal for a silent CLI-auto-update breakage (the stated F9 rationale, and the auto-updater is on) is lost.
findings.fix: Add a schema_mismatch classification when parse_stream_json sees well-formed JSON lines but no assistant-content line, distinct from no-JSON-at-all (saw_any_json already distinguishes these), plus the test.

findings.title: Orchestration lane reads config key 'models' that does not exist in kimi_adapter.v1.json
findings.evidence: _kimi_model_for_capability (run_agent_orchestration_task.py:669-688) does (json.loads(raw) or {}).get('models') on config/kimi_adapter.v1.json, but that file has no top-level 'models' key — it uses models_by_capability, models_by_role, default_model (kimi_adapter.v1.json:16-34). So models is always {} and the function always returns KIMI_HEADLESS_MODEL, making the capability->model mapping a silent no-op; the docstring's promise of a cheaper critic/summary model is never met. Masked in practice because the orchestration lane calls run_kimi with role='research' (:935) and passes the resolved model explicitly (:938), so the adapter's own models_by_capability resolution is bypassed too.
findings.fix: Read models_by_capability/models_by_role/default_model (or import kimi_adapter._resolve_model), or drop the redundant orchestration-side resolution and let the adapter resolve by passing model=None.

findings.title: Chain places the live repo tree in the critic's --add-dir, contrary to arch §3.5
findings.evidence: _run_kimi (agent_chain.py, added in 2a46f483b9) calls kimi_adapter.run_kimi with add_dirs=[REPO_ROOT, out_dir] for every role including 'critic'. build_argv emits a --add-dir for each (kimi_adapter.py:402-407), so the critic is granted --add-dir on the live C:/QM/repo tree. Arch §3.5 and contract §5.1 specify the critic --add-dir must be 'scratch dir only, with read access to the repo — never the live tree granted write'. Mitigated by the read-only agent-file (no Write/Edit/Bash) and the repo hash guard, but it deviates from the specified posture and relies entirely on the unverified assumption that --add-dir does not itself grant write.
findings.fix: For critic seats pass a read-scoped repo reference rather than the writable --add-dir live tree, or confirm/annotate via probe 4 that --add-dir is read-only and record that in the posture doc.

findings.title: Orchestration reads adapter result key 'returncode'; adapter returns 'rc'
findings.evidence: _run_kimi_slot reads result.get('returncode') (run_agent_orchestration_task.py:962), but kimi_adapter.run_kimi's result dict has no 'returncode' key — the exit code is under 'rc' (kimi_adapter.py:348-364). result.get('returncode') is therefore always None and the payload's returncode is always synthesized from status (0 if ok else 1); the adapter's real rc is dropped. Field-name seam; functionally masked.
findings.fix: Read result.get('rc') for the returncode.

findings.title: Research/creator Kimi role has unrestricted shell — authority guards are prompt-level, not the code-level guards the architecture claims
findings.evidence: For roles creator/research use_agent_file=false, read_only=false (kimi_adapter.v1.json:55-57). build_argv only attaches the tool-restricting --agent-file when use_agent_file is set (kimi_adapter.py:397-399), so research/creator runs get Kimi's default toolset INCLUDING Bash/Write (the probe battery only proved -p auto-runs Read/Write; nothing removes shell for non-critic roles, and the orchestration prompt itself instructs `python agent_router.py update-task ... --state REVIEW --verdict` and `python farmctl.py health`, which REQUIRE shell — run_agent_orchestration_task.py build_prompt kimi branch). The mutation guard fires only for critics: is_critic=read_only (kimi_adapter.py:555) and the critic_wrote conversion is gated `if is_critic and repo_write` (kimi_adapter.py:608); a research/creator repo write yields status ok with only a repo_write flag — asserted by test_creator_repo_write_flag_but_status_ok (test_kimi_adapter.py:299-306). The chain worsens this: _run_kimi passes add_dirs=[REPO_ROOT, out_dir] (the LIVE C:/QM/repo) to a non-read-only kimi creator (agent_chain.py _run_kimi), and resolve_creator accepts creator vendor=kimi with vendor_gate returning open in NORMAL. Consequently KIMI_INTEGRATION_ARCHITECTURE.md §4.2 'code-level guards (mechanical): No Kimi branch has a verdict-write path ... cannot invoke close-review ... independent of any prompt instruction' and 'no farmctl subcommand is callable by a Kimi task' / 'T_Live paths never in --add-dir' are FALSE for these roles: with shell, a prompt-injected or misbehaving run can execute `farmctl approve-card`, `agent_router close-review --state APPROVED`, write C:/QM/mt5/T_Live, or `git commit`. Capability omission (agent_router.py:1678-1680, TASK_TYPE_CAPABILITIES) only stops the ROUTER from ASSIGNING build/ops/verdict tasks; it does not confine the spawned process. The repo guard is detection-only, critic-only, and repo-only (never D:/QM or T_Live).
findings.fix: Give the research/creator kimi role the same --agent-file allowlist posture (deny Bash/PowerShell/Write/Edit) as the critic, or run it in an isolated worktree with the repo mounted read-only and D:/QM + C:/QM/mt5/T_Live absent from every reachable path; move the update-task REVIEW transition to the orchestrator (post-review) so kimi needs no shell. At minimum extend the mutation guard to the research role (fail the run on ANY repo/D:/QM/T_Live change, not just record a flag) and correct the architecture doc so it no longer claims mechanical enforcement that only the critic role actually has.

findings.title: Kimi CONSERVE never reaches either plane — the F4/R-G subscription-budget protection is inert
findings.evidence: kimi_governor._write_flag writes a fixed 4-line body (MANAGED_BY/set_at/reason/counts) with NO state field (kimi_governor.py:276-285), and reconcile_flag writes the flag ONLY on EXHAUSTED, clearing/leaving-absent on NORMAL and CONSERVE (kimi_governor.py:299-319). But both consumers key off a flag state: router kimi_quota_state does json.loads and treats any non-JSON present flag as EXHAUSTED, absent as NORMAL (agent_router.py kimi_quota_state), and chain _read_kimi_flag_state scans for a `state=` line and maps the MANAGED_BY-only body to EXHAUSTED (agent_chain.py:_read_kimi_flag_state). Net: when the governor computes CONSERVE (>=70% of a cap, or period-near-end) it writes NO flag, so router sees NORMAL and the chain gate is open. The CONSERVE machinery — KIMI_CONSERVE_CAPABILITIES narrowing + the route_once generic-research-strategy exclusion (agent_router.py route_once CONSERVE gate) and the chain critic-for-non-kimi-only branch — is unreachable. Only NORMAL and EXHAUSTED ever take effect. With gemini currently auth-degraded, kimi at cost_rank 12 therefore captures the generic research funnel up to the 100% cap with no CONSERVE brake, defeating the documented §5.2/§7.2 protection. (EXHAUSTED still works, but only by the fail-closed accident of an unparseable body.)
findings.fix: Make the governor the single source of the flag state: write the computed state (state=CONSERVE / state=EXHAUSTED, or a JSON {"state":...}) into KIMI_LOW_QUOTA.flag on BOTH CONSERVE and EXHAUSTED (and have router/chain read governor_state.json as the authority). Unify the flag encoding across kimi_governor, agent_router.kimi_quota_state and agent_chain._read_kimi_flag_state so CONSERVE is actually transmitted; add a test that a governor-produced CONSERVE flag narrows the router lane and gates chain creator/formatter kimi.

findings.title: Orchestration Plane-B lane does not honor KIMI_LOW_QUOTA=EXHAUSTED before spawning, contrary to §7.3
findings.evidence: _run_kimi_slot fetches agent_router.kimi_quota_state() only to record it in the result payload (run_agent_orchestration_task.py:874-892, 967); there is no gate on it, and the adapter honors only the QM_KIMI kill switch (kimi_adapter.py:485-491), never the KIMI_LOW_QUOTA flag. Architecture §7.3 states 'the orchestration branch checks the flag before spawning.' Plane A routing IS correctly disabled on EXHAUSTED (sync_default_registry sets enabled=False), so no NEW kimi tasks route, but a task already claimed IN_PROGRESS on kimi will still be spawned when EXHAUSTED. Budget-only impact; backtests unaffected.
findings.fix: Gate _run_kimi_slot (or the adapter) on kimi_quota_state()==EXHAUSTED (return a no-op result), so an in-flight kimi orchestration claim also stops under EXHAUSTED.

findings.title: Single-flight lock: a hard crash while holding leaks the lock for up to stale_s (2h); stored pid is never checked for liveness
findings.evidence: _acquire_single_flight steals a lock only when its timestamp is older than stale_s (kimi_adapter.py:206-217), with stale_s default 7200 (config single_flight.stale_s). The holder pid is written into the lock (kimi_adapter.py:203) but never used for liveness. Release is in a finally (kimi_adapter.py:602-603), so a normal exception releases, but a hard kill/crash leaves the lock; every subsequent Kimi call then waits wait_s (300s) and returns single_flight_busy for up to 2h. This is fail-safe (task left claimable, backtests untouched) and pid-reuse is NOT a correctness risk because liveness-by-pid is never tested — but the lane can stall unnecessarily. The stale-steal itself is race-safe: O_CREAT|O_EXCL ensures only one writer wins after concurrent unlinks.
findings.fix: Add a pid-liveness check to the stale path (steal immediately when the recorded pid is not a live process on this host), keeping the timestamp check as fallback, to shorten recovery after a crash.

notes: SAFETY/AUTHORITY verdicts. (1) 'No Kimi path can write agent_tasks/verdicts/work_items/holds/evidence or the repo' — PARTIALLY REFUTED. By design Kimi writes evidence artifacts and moves its OWN task to REVIEW with a task-level --verdict (intended, acceptable — REVIEW is non-authoritative). The protected authorities (pipeline verdict, APPROVED/PIPELINE/PASSED, close-review, farmctl mutations, work_items/holds) are code-enforced ONLY for the read-only critic role (agent-file removes shell). For the research/creator role (orchestration lane + chain creator) they are enforced by PROMPT TEXT ONLY because that role has full Bash — see finding 1. (2) 'No Kimi path reaches C:/QM/mt5/T_Live or AutoTrading' — code-level TRUE only in the sense that T_Live is never placed in --add-dir and no cap routes T_Live work to kimi; but since the research/creator role has Bash, T_Live is reachable via shell and is prevented only by the prompt. AutoTrading toggle is a MetaTrader UI action with no CLI path, so that remains OWNER-only regardless. (3) 'No farmctl mutation callable by a Kimi task' — TRUE for the critic (no shell); FALSE for research/creator (shell present). (4) Secrets — PROVEN clean: no credential contents are ever read, logged, printed, or ledgered; probe evidence scanned clean. (5) Single-flight lock — correct and race-safe; only weakness is slow recovery after a hard crash (finding 5), fail-safe direction. (6) Kill switches QM_KIMI=0 and QM_AGENT_CHAIN=0 — both correct and total across spawn paths. (7) Never-buy — PROVEN: no purchase code path. (8) Backtests unaffected when Kimi EXHAUSTED/missing — PROVEN. Secondary: the KIMI_LOW_QUOTA flag encoding is inconsistent across the three modules (finding 2) and the governor's own EXHAUSTED path works only by the routers' fail-closed accident; the QM_StrategyFarm_KimiGovernor_15min scheduled task from §8 is not added by the installer (acceptable because the adapter calls kimi_governor.record() inline per call). The default-OFF -IncludeKimi install and the probe-gated task installation materially limit the live exposure of finding 1 today, but the code path exists and should be closed before the lane is enabled."
